Subject: Re: Intermittent streaming chat slowness this morning

Hi Kimberly / Marissa,

We started seeing severe tail latency on the streaming chat on our evening peak (US-East) around 07:40 PT. p95 is elevated but p99 is the real problem — some agents experienced 5–8s latency on SSE frames and occasional dropped connections for high concurrency rooms. We attached a short log snippet and a Grafana screenshot from our SRE view. This is impacting our customer support SLAs.

Can Redwood please triage and let us know immediate mitigations? We do have a hard call with our CTO at 16:00 PT and I need an update before then.

— Tess

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Cc: dev_patel@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent streaming chat slowness this morning

Tess — thanks for the data and flagging. I pulled the metrics from our hosted API for the same window. We're seeing an uptick in open connections and a correlated jump in p99 for the SSE endpoint (/v1/streams/chat) in us-east-1 — from ~320ms baseline to ~2400–5200ms for top percentiles. Error rate (502/504) is also elevated for long-lived connections.

Immediate actions I'm spinning up now:
- Escalating to infra (Dev) to check node CPU/IO and our connection proxies.
- Increasing the streaming instance pool by +20% in the affected cluster as a short-term buffer.
- Enabling a fallback policy to a lower-concurrency routing tier (will impact throughput but reduce tail).

Can you confirm the volume patterns on your side (concurrent rooms, typical seq length)? That will help us tune batching and KV cache TTLs.

— Marissa, Customer Success (Redwood)

On Tue, Jun 29, 2027 at 09:28, marissa_cole@redwood.ai wrote:
> Tess — thanks for the data and flagging. I pulled the metrics from our hosted API for the same window. We're seeing an uptick in open connections and a correlated jump in p99 for the SSE endpoint (/v1/streams/chat) in us-east-1 — from ~320ms baseline to ~2400–5200ms for top percentiles. Error rate (502/504) is also elevated for long-lived connections.

Confirming initial triage findings:
- We observe connection bursts coincident with AcmeHealth's bulk agent shift at 07:30 PT. The majority of p99 spikes correlate with long-lived sessions that exceed 30s without client heartbeats.
- Nginx-based proxy ingress shows increased worker queue latency; KV cache hit rate drops during same windows indicating frequent cold prefix behavior.

Short-term mitigations implemented (@10:00 PT):
1) Added +4 streaming workers to the affected pool.
2) Reduced default keepalive timeout from 60s to 30s for SSE to reclaim stale connections faster.
3) Enabled conservative batching (batch max_tokens=256, batch_timeout=30ms) for the next 2 hours.

We will monitor p95/p99 for 30–60 minutes and follow up. If this does not stabilize, next step is a targeted routing policy to move Acme traffic to a dedicated lower-latency shard.

— Dev (Infra)

Kimberly / Team — thanks for the quick triage. A few items for the exec summary and the post-incident plan:

1) Short executive summary (1–2 bullets):
- Root cause (hypothesis): sudden concurrent session surge + long sequence lengths exposing cold-prefix and ingress proxy saturation, producing elevated p99 and periodic connection resets.
- Customer impact: increased p99 (up to ~5s) and temporary elevated 5xx for a subset of long-lived sessions during their peak shift; mitigated by instance scale-up and keepalive tuning.

2) Immediate remediation (what we did):
- +20% pool capacity +4 streaming workers; reduced SSE keepalive; enabled conservative batching temporarily.

3) Short-term prevention (next 48h):
- Proactive routing: allow us to offer an opt-in dedicated shard for AcmeHealth for peak windows (requires org approval).
- KV prefetch: implement a short-lived prefetch for known prefixes for high-concurrency users to reduce cold cache penalties (target: 12–24h rollout).
- Connection policing: soft connection caps per-API-key with graceful backoff hints (configurable).

4) Long-term proposal (costed):
- Dedicated shard (reserved capacity) with guaranteed latency targets for support-heavy customers. Estimate: 4–6 weeks to provision + validation; includes pricing uplift and a migration runbook.

Marissa — please finalize the one-slide and the 48h MOP. I will join the 16:00 PT CTO call for the exec overview.

— Stephanie
